claims.text: Low's memorandum of 9 August 1966 stated the study would be 'conducted almost entirely by non-believers' and would present 'the image of a group of non-believers trying their best to be objective but having an almost zero expectation of finding a saucer'; it became public in July 1967 when James E. McDonald found it in project files.

claims.sourceText: Robert J. Low memorandum to University of Colorado administrators, 9 August 1966
claims.text: 'The trick would be, I think, to describe the project so that, to the public, it would appear a totally objective study but, to the scientific community, would present the image of a group of nonbelievers.'

The same memo states the study 'would be conducted almost entirely by nonbelievers' who 'could and probably would add an impressive body of thick evidence that there is no reality to the observations.'
